meta.title: Interactive periodic table
meta.description: All 118 elements with data verified against IUPAC, PubChem and NIST: heat maps, states by temperature, a comparison view and a molar mass calculator. Works offline.

calculator.title: Molar mass calculator
calculator.intro: Type a formula with parentheses, brackets or hydrates. Counts go after the symbol; a middle dot, asterisk or period separates the water of hydration.
calculator.label: Chemical formula
calculator.approximate: Includes elements without a standard atomic weight: the mass number of the most stable isotope was used, so the result is approximate.
calculator.empty: Type a formula to see its molar mass and composition.

trends.title: Periodic trends
trends.intro: Properties change in an orderly way across the table. Pick one to see which way it increases.

electronegativity.title: Electronegativity
electronegativity.body: It is an atom's tendency to attract electrons in a bond. It increases across a period because nuclear charge grows while electrons stay in the same shell, and decreases down a group because valence electrons sit farther from the nucleus. Fluorine is the most electronegative.

atomicRadius.title: Atomic radius
atomicRadius.body: Going down a group adds electron shells, so atoms grow. Across a period nuclear charge increases and pulls the same shell in more tightly, so atoms shrink.

ionizationEnergy.title: Ionization energy
ionizationEnergy.body: It is the energy needed to remove the outermost electron. It follows the opposite trend to radius: the closer and more tightly held the electron, the harder it is to remove. Noble gases have the highest value in each period.

metallic.title: Metallic character
metallic.body: Metals give up electrons easily, so metallic character grows where ionization energy is low: the bottom left. A diagonal of metalloids separates metals from nonmetals.

grid.label: Periodic table of the elements
grid.keyboardHint: Use the arrow keys to move and Enter to open the details.
